title: Gas Log Set vs Gas Insert — Sales Script & Reference
description: Canonical comparison + sales script extracted from May 15 2026 Leo walk-in customer transcript (Drew + Jonathan tag-team sale). This is the most common 'I want to convert my wood fireplace to gas' conversation. Use in BSFA Smart Context when customer indicates gas-conversion intent.
source_transcripts: May 15 at 3 27 PM (Leo walk-in - gas log set conversation Rockford).txt (live customer transcript)
decision_question: Customer wants gas conversion in existing fireplace. Are they buying ambiance or heat?

gas_log_set.heat_type: radiant (heats objects + skin, 10-15 ft into room)
gas_log_set.heat_capacity: warms area in front of fireplace, NOT whole room
gas_log_set.operation: Operates same as burning wood — DOORS OPEN, DAMPER OPEN when burning
gas_log_set.fireplace_keeps: Existing fireplace walls + black trim + factory finish all stay
gas_log_set.log_customization: Top logs can be moved within base diagram; base logs must follow manufacturer diagram (controls flame travel + prevents sooting)
gas_log_set.preferred_display_per_drew_apr25: Most popular log style on display — 'glows more' than alternatives
gas_log_set.popularity_note: On display: 30% efficient, feels heat 15 feet away. Other log styles produce same heat + same flame size but don't glow as much

gas_insert.heat_type: convection (blower pulls cold air from floor, heats it, pushes out top)
gas_insert.heat_capacity: 1,500-2,000 sq ft, ~80% efficient (Drew quote: 'like home furnaces — like getting another furnace')

includes: venting system through existing pipes + new cap

anatomy: Sealed gas unit that slides into existing opening
Own venting system goes up through existing chimney + new cap
Two burners on premium units (front + back — turn off back burner to reduce heat)
gas_insert.operation: Fully sealed appliance — doors come off existing fireplace, panel surrounds the insert
gas_insert.installation_complexity: More involved than log set (venting + cap + opening modification)
gas_insert.lock_in_to_vendor: You are at the mercy of the gas insert manufacturer — only their logs work, set up to specific diagram, cannot be moved
gas_insert.thermal_efficiency_pitch: These are like home furnaces. In some situations cheaper to heat your house with this than the whole furnace (depends on electric vs gas heat baseline)
gas_insert.vendors: Travis, Mendota, Enviro, Kozy Heat, Kingsman, Lopi all carried

key_differentiators_for_customer.insert: Convection (warms whole room, can heat house in some cases)

key_differentiators_for_customer.log_set: Localized — sitting in front of fireplace
More realistic — open fire, no glass between you and flame
key_differentiators_for_customer.insert: Looks beautiful + ceramic glass front; less 'real wood' look but very polished

key_differentiators_for_customer.log_set: Doors open + damper open when burning (just like wood)
key_differentiators_for_customer.insert: Fully sealed — doors come off, panel surrounds it

key_differentiators_for_customer.log_set: More freedom — different log styles, mix-and-match (within base diagram)
key_differentiators_for_customer.insert: Locked to manufacturer — their logs, their layout, their specs

drew_sales_script_for_gas_log_set: It operates the same as if you're burning wood. Doors open, damper open when it's running.
The logs have a lifetime warranty — they're ceramic. They may eventually crumble over years, but Hargrove warranties them for life.
Burner is 5 years, valve and electronics are 3 years.
It looks realistic because there's no glass in front of it. It's an open fire.
It radiates heat 10-15 feet into the room — heats objects and skin. It's not convection heat.
Main purpose is ambiance. It looks pretty and warms the area in front of it.
All-in cost with gas run, installation, and remote — around $3,000 after tax. Could be less.
drew_sales_script_for_gas_insert: These are powerful heaters. I cannot stress that enough — their main purpose is heating. They look beautiful as well, but they're heaters.
It's an actual unit that slides into your opening. It has its own venting system that goes up through your existing pipes with a new cap.
These average 1,500-2,000 sq ft of heating. They're like home furnaces. About 80% efficient.
They have fan kits — blower system that pulls room air in for convection. Cold air sits on the floor, so it pulls air in down low, heats it, and spits it out up top.
The two-burner models let you turn off the back burner if you want less heat. Or you can control flame height with the remote.
Out-the-door install price: low end $7,000, high-end $10,000-$11,000.
In some situations, it's cheaper to heat your house with this than running your whole furnace — depends on whether you have electric or gas heat.

common_customer_questions.log_set_answer: Yes — within a base diagram. Top logs you can move around. Base logs follow a manufacturer pattern that controls flame travel and prevents sooting.
common_customer_questions.insert_answer: No — you're at the mercy of the manufacturer. Only their logs, set up to their diagram.

common_customer_questions.shared_answer: No — these are vented. The gas burns and goes up the chimney/vent. No harmful exhaust in the room.

common_customer_questions.log_set_answer: Doors are open when burning. When it's off, you can shut them. Damper is also always open when burning — just like burning wood.
common_customer_questions.insert_answer: Insert is fully sealed — the existing doors come off, and a panel surrounds the new unit. Sealed gasketed glass.

common_customer_questions.q: How much heat does it actually produce?
common_customer_questions.log_set_answer: Heats objects and skin in front of it. ~10-15 feet of warm zone. Not for heating a whole room.

common_customer_questions.shared_answer: If it's in stock, about 3-4 weeks. Once you put a down payment in, the countdown starts.
Quote is guaranteed for 30 days from save date in BisTrack.

Customer financing via Synchrony or Wells Fargo — link on Benson website
Oralba (receptionist x100) helps walk customers through financing process

21" is a common gas log set size (sized to existing fireplace opening)
